title: Surat Steps Up Diwali Food Checks, Seizes 398 Kg of Paneer
excerpt: SMC officials sampled sweets at 16 outlets on Tuesday and seized nearly 400 kg of paneer from a Bamroli Road dairy unit, inside the FSSAI's national festive drive.
body:
• Surat Municipal Corporation food safety officials inspected 16 sweet outlets on Tuesday and collected 31 samples of sweets and desserts for laboratory testing.
  • A day earlier, officials and police seized 398 kg of low-fat paneer worth about Rs 1.11 lakh from a dairy unit on New Bamroli Road and issued hygiene notices.
  • Results of the seized paneer samples are expected within the next couple of days, and further action depends on the laboratory findings.
  • The checks sit inside a national festive-season drive ordered by the FSSAI on September 29 covering sweets, dairy, edible oils and savouries.

Surat's municipal food safety department has stepped up inspections across the city ahead of Diwali, when demand for sweets and festive foods surges. On Tuesday, officials inspected 16 outlets selling sweets and collected 31 samples of sweets and desserts for laboratory testing, The Times of India reported.

The drive covered popular sweet shops across Surat. Officials described the checks as routine festive-season enforcement meant to stop substandard or unsafe food reaching residents at the time of year when sweets are bought in the largest quantities.

398 kg of paneer seized on Monday

"Officials collected paneer samples, issued notices over hygiene deficiencies found during the inspection, and seized 398 kg of low-fat paneer estimated to be worth about Rs 1.11 lakh."

On Monday, the food safety department, working with the police, inspected Ms Amrut Milk and Milk Products on New Bamroli Road, near Tirupati Circle. Officials collected paneer samples, issued notices over hygiene deficiencies found during the inspection, and seized 398 kg of low-fat paneer estimated to be worth about Rs 1.11 lakh.

The paneer samples have been sent to a laboratory for testing. Officials said results are expected within the next couple of days, and that further action will follow the laboratory findings and the unit's compliance with food safety regulations.

Part of a national festive drive

Surat's checks follow a special festive drive directed by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) on September 29, 2026, which asked food safety commissioners in every state and union territory to run heightened surveillance through Navratri and Diwali. The directive targets the foods most at risk of adulteration in the festive rush — milk and milk products such as ghee, khoa and paneer, sweets, snacks and savouries, edible oils and beverages — and asks enforcement teams to deploy Food Safety on Wheels mobile laboratories in prominent marketplaces for on-the-spot testing.

The same national drive has produced enforcement actions elsewhere, including in Haryana, where unsafe paneer was destroyed as Diwali sweet checks intensified.

What shoppers should do

The practical takeaway for anyone buying mithai this week: buy from FSSAI-registered vendors, and treat unusually cheap paneer, khoa and ghee as a warning sign rather than a bargain. Festive demand is exactly when adulterated stock enters the market, which is why the sampling drives run in the days just before Diwali rather than after it.
